currentContext.strengths: Holding-company support structure: the Company has no employees and its Key Managerial Personnel are deputed by Lodha Developers Limited, and it relies on group-level frameworks - the Lodha cyber-security incident report process and the group anti-money-laundering / anti-bribery / anti-corruption policy hosted on the holding company's website.

There was no change in the authorised or paid-up share capital during FY 2025-26. currentContext.mdna: CONTEXT FLAG: the MD&A demand narrative below is about the Indian real estate INDUSTRY, not the Company's own revenue - the same MD&A states 'The Company does not have any project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in near future.'|Management believes India is 'only in the early stages of a multi decade housing upcycle', with a large and growing population, strong economy, high single-digit wage growth and urbanisation expected to drive housing demand.|Structural demand drivers and industry dynamics are expected to generate significant housing demand and to translate into 'robust pre-sales in the years ahead'.|Anticipated interest-rate reductions and government-led tax rebates are expected to provide additional impetus to the affordable and mid-income housing segments.|A visible shift in customer preference towards branded developers, recognising the importance of execution capability; residential markets across top Indian cities are entering a phase of greater maturity with more measured growth, increased competition among branded developers and a focus on timely execution, quality and affordability.|Macro backdrop stated: the Indian economy is projected to grow by 6.6% in FY27 versus 7.7% in FY26 (RBI also expects around 6.6% in FY27), with the slowdown attributed to higher crude prices in the aftermath of the Iran-USA war; retail inflation has hardened to 3.9% in May-26 versus 2.8% in May-25.|Management flags the counter-case it does not endorse: 'there are concerns of this being the peak of the cycle and demand softening going forward', which it counters with India's need for quality housing and low home-ownership capability levels.

risks.risk: No operating business and no pipeline - the Company is effectively dormant
risks.note: The Board's Report states: 'The Company's real estate project was completed in 2018. The Company does not have any ongoing business operations and does not intend to undertake any new real estate development project. The Company trades in building and construction materials.' The MD&A repeats twice that the Company 'does not have any project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in near future'. Everything the MD&A says about housing demand therefore describes an industry the Company no longer participates in.

risks.risk: Total customer / counterparty concentration on the holding company
risks.note: BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 9 ('Open-ness of business') discloses Share of RPTs - Sales to related parties as a percentage of total sales at 100% in FY 2026 versus 40% in FY 2025, with sales to dealers/distributors NIL and no trading houses used. Loans and advances given to related parties were 100% of total loans and advances in FY 2025 and NIL in FY 2026. The revenue base is thus a single related counterparty.

risks.risk: Complete dependence on the holding company for management capacity
risks.note: 'The Company does not have any employee. The KMPs are deputed by the holding company.' The BRSR adds that the Company has no employees or workers, that directors draw no remuneration from the Company, and that governance frameworks (anti-bribery policy, cyber-security incident process) sit at Lodha group level. The Company has no independent operating organisation.

risks.risk: Pending merger by absorption into Lodha Developers Limited - the listed entity may cease to exist
risks.note: The Board's Report discloses that an application for a Scheme of Merger by Absorption with holding company Lodha Developers Limited was filed before the NCLT, Mumbai Bench on June 11, 2026 under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013. No timeline, swap ratio or approval status is stated in the supplied text; the report points to the notes to the financial statements for further detail.

risks.risk: Sector labour intensity and input-cost / land-price inflation
risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns: 'The real estate sector is heavily dependent on manpower. There is a need for development of technologically less labour-intensive alternative methods of construction. Further, the increase in land prices, inputs costs are risks to the industry.'

risks.risk: Interest-cost and liquidity risk to demand and margins
risks.note: MD&A: 'Higher interest cost would dent margins and may have a direct effect on the customer's cash flow as well. Increase in end product prices coupled with tight liquidity may impact demand.'

risks.risk: Tax and levy burden compressing margins
risks.note: MD&A: 'The various taxes and levies would add to the costs and this is likely to squeeze margins as end product prices may not go up correspondingly.' The cautionary statement further names changes in government regulations and tax regimes, material availability and prices, and cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets as factors that could make actual results differ materially.

risks.risk: Unresolved disputed tax and legal claims (back-filled with provenance)
risks.note: BACK-FILLED from the notes to the financial statements, which appear in the profile and governance_entities sibling bundles and not in this one: contingent liabilities are disclosed as 'Claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts' in two buckets - Disputed Taxation Matters and Disputed Other Legal Cases (amounts deliberately not reproduced). The note states the contingent liabilities exclude the undeterminable outcome of pending litigations, and that the Company has assessed that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is not probable.

risks.risk: Governance concentration - a peak-cycle warning management itself records
risks.note: MD&A Opportunities: 'Because housing has been in a secular uptrend over the last 4-5 years, there are concerns of this being the peak of the cycle and demand softening going forward.' Management states its own belief that India is 'only in the early stages of a multi decade housing upcycle', so the downside case is acknowledged but not adopted.
